cohort: The study included 406 postpartum women aged 18-45 years with singleton pregnancies and a gestational age of at least 37 weeks, followed at Rajavithi Hospital.
finding: The incidence of self-reported urinary incontinence was 39% at 2 days postpartum, decreasing to 0% by 6 months, with caffeine consumption during pregnancy being the only identified risk factor.
mod_finding: Delivery type was adjusted for in the analysis but was not found to be a significant risk factor for urinary incontinence.
birth_weight: N/A (measured but no specific range/criteria beyond being full-term)
